info.title: Brainixa Backend - Session Changelog API (update-16)
info.description:
A CHANGELOG, not a full reference: it documents what each update batch added or changed, so endpoints untouched since the base version are deliberately absent.

Every tag reads `<batch> / <Role> / <Feature>`, and the batch is the one that LAST touched that operation - an endpoint added in update-2 and changed in update-5 is tagged update-5, with its history kept in the summary. Filter by `update-5` to see this batch alone.

`old` through `update-4` are inherited from the Najeh codebase this platform was built from. `update-5` is Brainixa's own first batch: the payment gateway, the question bank, and the fixes around them. The prose summary of that batch is `updates-for-project/API_UPDATE_5_SUMMARY.md`.

Business-logic errors come back with HTTP 200 and `status: "error"` in the body. Branch on `status`, not on the HTTP code.

`update-6` ports the consultation and package-session cycle from the Najeh codebase, WITHOUT its platform-owner idea: Brainixa has no owner who gives sessions without being a teacher, so every slot here belongs to a real teacher and there is no teacher_id = 0 anywhere. It adds a meeting link to consultations, start and end as a stored state for both consultations and package sessions, an admin way to approve or refuse a booking, and scopes a student's calendar to the packages they actually hold. Migrations 107 to 109.

`update-7` is the live-class batch and the loose ends around it: Zoom played inside the platform for all three kinds of live meeting (the weekly class sessions, the dated package appointments and the 1:1 consultations), a manual-sales sheet for admin and teacher, a chat contact directory read from the real tables instead of Firebase's stale copy, and hero slides as a table of their own.

update-7 also turns the books library into a STORE. No products table was added: `course_books.file_type` carries `physical` for an item with no file, so every existing book endpoint sells one unchanged. Clients branch on that field rather than assuming a file exists.

`update-8` (FIX): GET /student/exams leaked unit-scoped exams into the general listing whenever the request carried no `course_id` at all - the documented "whole-course exams only by default" rule was only ever enforced when `course_id` was explicitly passed. A student's general exams tab (no filters) could show a unit exam mixed in with the whole-course/standalone ones. The same default - `unit_id IS NULL` unless `include_unit_exams`/`with_unit_exams` says otherwise - now applies regardless of whether `course_id` is present. No response shape change, no new field; strictly fewer rows come back from the general (no-filter) call than before. A unit's own exams remain fully visible from inside that unit's content (GET /student/courses .../units, unaffected - that endpoint always filtered by `unit_id` directly).

`update-13` is the Report Center (مركز التقارير): the four reports an owner asked to be pulled automatically rather than compiled by hand - sales, live-class attendance for both students and teachers, payroll with its deductions, and the after-class ratings - each over a `date_from`/`date_to` range and each downloadable as .xlsx. No migration: every figure already existed in rows the platform writes, and each report delegates to the module that already owns its numbers, so none of them can drift from the Sales screen, the attendance report or the ratings summary. Payroll is the one report with queries of its own, because the wallet had a ledger and a balance but never a per-period payslip; it is gated on `manage_wallets` rather than `manage_reports`.

`update-14` gives the store products of its own. Until now everything it sold was a `course_books` row with no file attached, which works for a printed book and for nothing else - a school bag has no subject, no course and no unit, and the only category on that table says whether a PDF is a summary or a past paper. `products` and `product_categories` are new tables, deliberately separate from books and from course categories, and `GET /store` is the one place the two are shown side by side, each entry carrying `item_type` because an id is unique only within its own type. Nothing existing changed: no column was added to `course_books` and `GET /books` lists them exactly as before. Migration 127. Buying a product is NOT part of this batch - the catalogue is.

`update-14` also lets a product carry a file of any type (migration 128). `upload_any_file()` inverts the usual allow-list and refuses only what a web server might execute, checking every segment of the name so a double extension does not slip past; `uploads/.htaccess` already disables execution in that directory, so the deny-list is the first lock rather than the only one. `file_is_public` decides whether the shop front is given the path at all, and defaults to withholding it.

servers.description: Whatever the Postman environment points at

StudentAuth.description: Student role JWT (some endpoints accept this OPTIONALLY, falling back to ?student_id=)

AnyAuth.description: Any ONE of admin/teacher/student/parent JWTs, tried in that order

PaginatedResponse.description: update-3 (CORRECTION): the real pagination envelope returned by the backend. Earlier revisions of this file wrongly documented a `meta {page, limit, total}` object that no endpoint has ever returned.

statistics.description: Only present on endpoints that compute aggregate counters; omitted otherwise.

HrPolicySettings.description: update-3 (NEW): the single global HR/attendance policy row (`hr_policy_settings`, always id = 1). Every limit, fine and default pay value in the system is read fresh from here at the moment a decision is made, so edits never apply retroactively.

id.description: Always 1 - this table holds exactly one row by design (enforced by a CHECK constraint).

teacher_max_absence_with_permission_per_.description: How many EXCUSED absences a teacher may take per calendar month. Informational/reporting limit - excused absences are already exempt from fines and from the suspension counter.

teacher_max_absence_without_permission.description: Unexcused absences per calendar month before the teacher is auto-flagged `is_attendance_suspended = 1`. Counted from the 1st of the current month.

teacher_max_reschedule_per_month.description: Reschedule requests a teacher may submit per calendar month; the (N+1)th POST /teacher/sessions/reschedule-request is rejected.

teacher_grace_minutes.description: Minutes after the scheduled start within which a teacher check-in still counts as `present`. Beyond it the occurrence becomes `late` and (if not excused) is fined per minute.

teacher_late_fine_per_minute.description: Charged as minutes_late x this value when a teacher checks in late without an approved late_notice. Set to 0 to disable late fines entirely.

teacher_absence_fine_amount.description: Flat fine applied by the cron for a full unexcused no-show. Set to 0 to disable absence fines entirely.

student_max_absence_with_permission_per_.description: Student mirror of the teacher field. Students are never fined - only counted.

student_max_absence_without_permission.description: Unexcused absences per calendar month before the student's subscription is auto-frozen (`student_subscriptions.is_active = 0`).

student_max_reschedule_per_month.description: Reschedule requests a student may submit per calendar month; the (N+1)th POST /student/sessions/reschedule-request is rejected.

student_grace_minutes.description: Minutes after the scheduled start within which a student check-in still counts as `present`.

default_pay_model.description: Used for any teacher with no row in `teacher_pay_rates`.

default_pay_rate.description: The amount that goes with default_pay_model.

TeacherPayRate.description: update-3 (NEW): the effective pay rate for one teacher. This object ALWAYS resolves to something - if the teacher has no personal override row, the values fall back to the global defaults from HrPolicySettings, so the client never has to merge them itself.

TeacherWalletTransaction.description: update-3 (NEW): one immutable row of the teacher wallet ledger (`teacher_wallet_transactions`). Rows are never edited or deleted - a reversal is a new compensating row - so the ledger is a complete audit trail and the sum of `amount` always equals `teachers.wallet_balance`.

type.description: `earning` = pay credited at session check-out. `fine` = automatic deduction (lateness or unexcused absence). `refund` = money returned after an approved appeal. `admin_adjustment` = manual admin correction, either direction.

amount.description: SIGNED. Positive = credit (earning / refund / positive adjustment). Negative = debit (fine / negative adjustment). Display the absolute value with a +/- indicator derived from this sign, do not assume fines are positive.

reference_id.description: class_sessions.id for `session`, teacher_deduction_appeals.id for `appeal`, null for `manual`.

note.description: Human-readable Arabic reason, e.g. 'خصم تأخير 12 دقيقة' or 'أجر حصة'. For admin_adjustment this is the mandatory note the admin typed.

created_by_id.description: The admin id when created_by_type = 'admin'; null when the system wrote the row.

can_appeal.description: update-3: convenience flag present ONLY on the teacher-facing GET /teacher/wallet/transactions. True exactly when type = 'fine'. Use it to decide whether to render the 'Appeal' button; the server still re-validates, and also rejects a second appeal on the same transaction.

AttendanceExceptionRequest.description: update-3 (NEW): one absence-with-permission or late-notice request (`attendance_exception_requests`). The exact same object shape is returned to the teacher, the student and the admin - only the `requester` sub-object differs by role.

occurrence_date.description: The specific calendar date this request covers. class_sessions rows are WEEKLY RECURRING templates (one row per weekday/time), so a request is always pinned to one occurrence, never to the whole series.

request_type.description: `absence_permission` = 'I will miss this occurrence entirely'. `late_notice` = 'I will attend but arrive late'.

expected_minutes_late.description: Required and > 0 for late_notice; null for absence_permission.

session.description: The fully resolved class session object (same shape used across the sessions endpoints), embedded so no second call is needed to render the row.

requester.description: The person who filed it. For a student: {id, name, email, image}. For a teacher the same plus {is_active, is_attendance_suspended} - so the admin review screen can see at a glance whether this teacher is already attendance-suspended.

TeacherDeductionAppeal.description: update-3 (NEW): a teacher's objection to one `fine` wallet transaction (`teacher_deduction_appeals`). At most one appeal per transaction, ever.

teacher.description: {id, name, email, image} of the appealing teacher.

TeacherWalletRow.description: update-3 (NEW): one teacher as shown on the admin 'teacher wallets' screen - identity, both status flags, cached balance and effective pay rate in a single row, so that screen needs no per-teacher follow-up calls.

is_active.description: The ADMIN's manual enable/disable switch. 0 here means the teacher genuinely cannot log in.

is_attendance_suspended.description: update-3 (NEW column, migration 061): set automatically by the attendance policy. Does NOT block login - render it as a separate 'attendance-suspended' badge, never as 'Inactive'. Clear it with POST /admin/teacher-wallets/lift-suspension.

wallet_balance.description: Cached sum of every ledger row for this teacher.

FrozenStateFlags.description: update-3 (NEW, added to several student-facing objects): tells 'frozen because of the attendance policy' apart from 'expired' and from 'never subscribed'. A subscription's is_active is ONLY ever set to 0 by the attendance auto-freeze, so is_frozen is unambiguous. Render it as 'مجمد' (Frozen), NOT as 'غير فعال' (Inactive), and offer a contact-support action.

is_frozen.description: true when the subscription/course access exists but is currently frozen for excessive unauthorized absence (is_active = 0 AND not expired).

freeze_reason.description: Localized, ready-to-display explanation when is_frozen is true; null otherwise. Arabic: 'تم تجميد اشتراكك تلقائيًا لتجاوزك الحد المسموح به من الغياب بدون إذن...'.

ExamSummary.description: One exam from `course_exams`. EVERY exam always carries a non-null `course_id` (the admin/teacher UI requires picking a course to create any exam) - `unit_id` is what distinguishes a unit-scoped exam from a whole-course exam, it is null for the latter.

course_id.description: Always set in practice - see the type description.

unit_id.description: null = whole-course exam. Set = this exam belongs to one specific unit inside course_id.

is_active.description: update-4 (CLARIFIED): this IS the 'show exam to students' toggle - GET /student/exams filters on is_active = 1, so an admin/teacher setting this to 0 (via PUT /admin/exams or PUT /teacher/exams) immediately hides the exam from every student, with no other side effect. See also the explicit alias `show_to_students` below.

unit.description: update-3 (NEW): lightweight {id, name}, present only when unit_id is set. Lets the client label/group unit exams without a second lookup per row.

course.description: update-3 (NEW): full course details (same shape as elsewhere in the API), present whenever course_id is set - i.e. on every exam in practice.

subject.description: update-3 (NEW): full subject details, present only when subject_id is set (rare - most exams are scoped to a course or a unit, not a bare subject).

my_attempt.description: The calling student's own attempt at this exam, if any: {id, status, total_score, max_score}. null if they have never started it.

show_to_students.description: update-4 (NEW): explicit alias of `is_active` for this exam, added so the show/hide-to-students semantics don't have to be inferred from a generically-named `is_active` field. Always equal to `is_active`.

TeacherHomeResponse.description: update-4 (REWRITE): the teacher dashboard home screen. Every field is computed live from the DB - the previous version of this endpoint returned hardcoded demo data (fake KPI numbers, a fixed 7-month chart, 3 made-up 'recent activity' rows) whenever the real query came back empty; none of that placeholder behavior remains.

teacher.description: Core profile snapshot for the header. NOTE: this is a lighter object than GET /teacher/auth/profile (no city/experience/qualifications/metrics) - fetch that endpoint separately for the full profile screen.

rating.description: Real average from `teachers.rating`, which is recomputed on every new approved student rating - not a placeholder.

reviews_count.description: COUNT of approved rows in `teacher_ratings` for this teacher.

is_attendance_suspended.description: Section 10 automatic attendance restriction - separate from is_active, never blocks login (see the account-suspension notes on other endpoints).

subjects.description: Every subject this teacher is assigned to, from get_teacher_subjects_details().

kpis.description: Single-number summary cards for the top of the dashboard - every value also appears in more detail further down in the response (wallet, today, pending_actions).

total_students.description: Distinct students subscribed to this teacher directly, or to any course/subject they teach.

total_courses.description: Courses/packages this teacher owns or is linked to (course_teachers), active only.

total_active_sessions.description: Count of this teacher's active weekly class_sessions rows (their whole recurring schedule, not just today).

pending_actions_count.description: Sum of every counter in `pending_actions` - use this for a single badge/notification-dot.

wallet.description: Section 10 (attendance/salary system) snapshot - same numbers as GET /teacher/wallet, embedded here to save the home screen a second call.

sessions.description: Full session detail objects for every one of the teacher's active class_sessions scheduled today - same shape and same status/is_available_now/meeting_link logic as GET /teacher/sessions, so a client already rendering that screen can reuse its card component here unchanged.

pending_actions.description: Everything currently waiting on this teacher, broken out so the UI can deep-link each count to its own screen.

pending_homework_grading_count.description: homework_submissions with status='submitted' for homework this teacher created.

pending_exam_grading_count.description: exam_attempts with status='submitted' (i.e. containing at least one written question awaiting manual grading) for exams this teacher owns - same ownership rule as teacher_owns_exam().

incoming_reschedule_requests_count.description: Pending session_reschedule_requests filed BY a student, addressed to this teacher (see PUT /teacher/sessions/reschedule-requests/review).

my_attendance_exception_requests_pending.description: This teacher's OWN absence/late-notice requests still awaiting admin review (Section 10).

my_deduction_appeals_pending_count.description: This teacher's OWN wallet-deduction appeals still awaiting admin review (Section 10).

consultation_requests_pending_count.description: consultation_slots booked by a student but not yet approved/rejected by this teacher.

total_count.description: Sum of all six counters above - identical to kpis.pending_actions_count.

my_courses.description: Up to 6 of this teacher's courses/packages (same objects as GET /teacher/courses), each additionally carrying `students_count` (real count of active subscriptions covering that specific course).

upcoming_consultations.description: Up to 5 upcoming consultation slots that are booked AND approved (status='approved'), from today onward, ordered by date/time. A slot merely requested (status='pending') shows up in pending_actions.consultation_requests_pending_count instead, not here.

recent_notifications.description: The 5 most recent notifications for this teacher (newest first) - a preview; use GET /teacher/notifications for the full paginated inbox.

DashboardSalesSource.description: One revenue channel. The four channels together make up every figure in `sales`.

key.description: `online_payments` = paid rows in payment_transactions (EasyKash purchases of a course or a book). `subscription_codes` = every row in code_redemptions_log, valued at subscription_codes.price. `offline_book_grants` = student_book_subscriptions rows with price > 0 that an admin/teacher created by hand - rows that came from an online purchase are excluded here (they are matched through payment_transactions.granted_ref_id) so a paid book is never counted twice. `legacy_transactions` = the old, no-longer-written `transactions` ledger; nothing inserts into it today, but historical rows in it were real money and are still included.

DashboardSales.description: Platform revenue. `total`/`today`/`this_month`/`this_year` are the SUM across all four channels in `sources`, so `total` always equals the sum of `sources[].total`.

currency.description: update-4: the platform prices everything in US dollars. `payment_transactions.currency` used to default to 'EGP' because the EasyKash gateway was wired up first, but no gateway is actually in use; migration 067 switches the column default to 'USD' and relabels existing rows, so revenue totals never sum two currencies into one number.

orders_total.description: Number of paid transactions across every channel, all time.

online_by_item.description: Split of the `online_payments` channel only, by what was bought.

manual_grants_without_price.description: Count of student_subscriptions an admin handed out by hand - no code, no payment. The schema stores no price for these, so they cannot appear in any revenue figure. The count is returned so that gap is visible instead of looking like missing money.

DashboardCourseSales.description: Sales of a single course, highest revenue first in the array (so index 0 is the best seller). Counts paid course rows in payment_transactions, code redemptions that unlock the course, and legacy transaction_items. A code that unlocks several courses has its price split evenly between them, so per-course revenue still adds up to the platform total.

price.description: The course's current list price, not what was earned.

link.description: Admin-dashboard route for this course, e.g. `/courses/12`.

DashboardActivityItem.description: One platform event. There is no audit-log table in this project - the feed is assembled on the fly from the newest rows of the tables that represent real events, merged and sorted by time. Every label comes in both languages so nothing has to be translated client-side, and DB enum values never reach the screen untranslated.

entity_id.description: Primary key of the row the event came from, within its own table.

link.description: Admin-dashboard route to open when the activity is clicked.

title_ar.description: Ready-to-display Arabic label for the event.

title_en.description: The same label in English - pick whichever matches the UI language.

description_ar.description: Who/what the event is about (person name, amount, translated status), in Arabic.

description_en.description: The same detail line in English.

status.description: Raw DB status of the underlying request (`pending` | `approved` | `rejected` | ...), present only on request-type events (`book_purchase_request`, `reschedule_request`, `attendance_exception_request`). It is already translated inside `description_ar`/`description_en`; this field is for filtering or colouring, not for display.

AvailabilityBooking.description: One student attached to a dated slot.

student_subscription_id.description: The subscription the booking was charged against, when one was found.

booked_by_type.description: Who performed the booking - a student booking themselves, or an admin/teacher doing it for them.

AvailabilitySlot.description:
update-4 (NEW): one teaching appointment on a REAL calendar date. This is a separate layer from `class_sessions`, which is a weekly recurring pattern (`day_of_week` + `start_time`) with no date on it and is unchanged. A slot with `capacity` 1 is a private appointment; a higher capacity makes it a group one - both use the same `bookings` array, there is no second mechanism.

update-7: the raw `zoom_meeting_id` and `zoom_password` are NEVER serialised onto a slot, for any role. A meeting number plus its password is enough to walk into the room from outside the platform, so the only way in is a signature minted by the Zoom join endpoints, against the caller's own entitlement.

capacity.description: How many students this slot accepts. 1 = private.

booked_count.description: Cached count of non-cancelled bookings, recomputed on every write.

is_bookable.description: True when status is 'available' and there is at least one place left.

status.description: 'full' is derived from capacity automatically; 'cancelled' and 'completed' are set explicitly and are never overwritten by the booking count.

day_of_week.description: Derived from slot_date, for display only.

started_at.description: update-6. When Start was pressed, if it was.

ended_at.description: update-6. When End was pressed. Beats everything else.

window_opens_at.description: update-6. Ten minutes before start_time on slot_date; the clock gate opens here.

window_closes_at.description: update-6. end_time on slot_date; the clock gate closes here.

is_live.description:
update-6. TRUE when the session is open to its students, and the ONLY thing a client should gate the meeting link on - not the clock it could read itself, and not the booking.

Two gates, either one opens it, and ended_at closes it over both:
  ended_at set           -> false, always
  started_at set         -> true (a person started it, possibly early)
  now within the window  -> true (the hour itself)

The clock is there because a teacher who forgets to press Start would otherwise lock out a room of students who arrived on time; the person is there because a forgotten End would leave the link open all night.

has_zoom.description: update-7 (NEW): a Zoom room has existed for this slot at some point. STICKY - the meeting id is never cleared on End, so this stays true once a room has been opened. Do not gate a Join button on it; use `zoom_is_live`.

zoom_is_live.description:
update-7 (NEW): a Zoom room is open RIGHT NOW (`has_zoom` and the slot has not been ended). This is the field a Join or End button should read.

Deliberately separate from `is_live`, which is a clock-window flag: `is_live` is true during the slot's own hour even if nobody has pressed Start, so a forgotten Start does not lock the students out of a plain meeting link. The two answer different questions.

is_student_booked.description: update-7 (NEW): only present when the list was asked for with `student_id` and `include_open=1`. Says whether THIS student is booked into the row, so open slots and that student's own slots can be told apart on one calendar.

AvailabilityPatternBody.description: A recurrence turned into one row per real date. Two hard caps protect the database: the range cannot exceed 400 days and a single request cannot produce more than 300 slots. Dates the teacher already has a slot for at that exact start_time are SKIPPED rather than failing the request, so re-running an overlapping range is safe.

days.description: Weekly pattern only - at least one weekday name.

days_of_month.description: Monthly pattern only. A month too short for the given day simply gets no slot that month rather than sliding into the next one.

StudentCertificate.description: One certificate awarded to one student. `course_id` is nullable: a certificate can be granted at any time without belonging to any course, which is what the admin grant screen does.

course_id.description: Copied from the certificate template; null when the certificate is not tied to a course.

certificate_code.description: Unique per issued certificate, generated on grant.

certificate.description: The certificate template this was issued from.

DiscountCode.description: update-4 (NEW): a code that REDUCES a price. It is not a `subscription_code`: a subscription code opens access outright and is free, while a discount code grants nothing at all on its own. They are separate tables so neither flow can accidentally hand out access or money.

code.description: Unique, upper-cased. Generated as `DISC-XXXXXXXX` when not supplied.

discount_value.description: Percent (max 100) or a fixed amount in USD.

max_discount_amount.description: Caps a percentage discount. Ignored for a fixed one.

applies_to.description: Derived from `course_ids`: sending courses makes it 'selected', clearing them makes it 'all', so the two can never contradict each other.

course_ids.description: Courses AND packages - a package is a course row.

used_count.description: Only real applications count; a price preview never increments it.

DiscountCheckResult.description: What a code would take off. Read-only - checking never consumes a use, so a student may check as often as they like.

message.description: Arabic, ready to display - says exactly why a code was refused (expired, exhausted, wrong course, already used by this student...).

code.description: A summary of the matched code (omitted when invalid).

discount_amount.description: Never exceeds the price - a discount can not turn a total negative.

claim_id.description: update-4: present only on POST /student/discount-codes/apply - the id of the pending claim, which is what DELETE /student/discount-codes/cancel takes.

status.description: update-4: `pending` after a student applies a code (the code's quota is untouched), `applied` once a grant has actually spent it. Absent on a plain read-only check.

DiscountClaim.description: update-4 (NEW): a code a student has pinned to a course and is still holding. It is a row on `discount_code_redemptions` with status `pending`, so it costs the code nothing until an admin grant promotes it.

id.description: The claim id - pass it to DELETE /student/discount-codes/cancel to drop it.

course.description: The course or package the claim is pinned to.

is_still_valid.description: False when the code stopped working AFTER the claim was made - deactivated, expired, or used up by other students. The claim is kept so the student can see what happened, but it will be refused at grant time, so do NOT render it as a live discount.

DiscountCodeInput.description: update-4 (NEW): the create/update body shared by the admin and teacher discount-code endpoints. On the teacher endpoints every id in `course_ids` must be one of that teacher's own courses.

code.description: Optional on create - left empty, one is generated. Cannot be changed afterwards.

discount_value.description: Must be greater than zero, and at most 100 for a percentage.

max_discount_amount.description: Caps a percentage discount. Ignored for a fixed one.

course_ids.description: Empty means the code is not tied to specific courses (`applies_to` becomes 'all'); for a TEACHER-owned code that means all of that teacher's courses, never the whole platform. Sending a list makes `applies_to` 'selected' and replaces the previous scope outright.

AppConfig.description: update-4: the flat operational config served by GET /app-config.

whatsapp_number.description: Digits only, with country code. Append to https://wa.me/. Empty when not configured.

social.description: Empty string means the platform has no link for that network - hide the icon.

registration_disabled_message.description: Already in the language of the request (Accept-Language). Show it as-is. Falls back to the other language rather than to an empty string when only one side has been filled in.

SalesOverview.description: Same shape as DashboardSales, with one addition: a new 'offline_payments' source covering APPROVED bank-transfer course purchases (offline_payment_requests). Before this, an approved offline course payment granted access through student_subscriptions - which has no price column at all - so that money was invisible in every total on the platform. Offline BOOK payments were already counted under 'offline_book_grants', since both paths write the same student_book_subscriptions row.

range.description: Present only when date_from/date_to were sent. today/this_month/this_year stay fixed reference points regardless of this filter.

SalesItem.description: One course, package or book's sales, aggregated across every revenue channel.

course_id.description: Present when kind is course or package.

price.description: Current list price, not what was earned.

link.description: Admin-dashboard route to open this item.

SalesTransaction.description: One individual sale behind an item's aggregate revenue on the Sales list.

reference.description: Whatever identifies this specific sale in its own channel - a payment reference, a subscription code, a bank transfer reference.

ConsultationSlot.description:
One consultation. Every slot belongs to a real teacher.

update-7: `zoom_meeting_id` and `zoom_password` are stripped before the row is sent, for every role.

meeting_link.description: update-6, migration 107. Where the consultation is held. Null on every row until that migration has run - the column is read behind an existence check, so the endpoint still answers.

status.description: available -> pending (a student booked) -> approved (admin or teacher agreed) -> in_progress (started) -> completed (ended). A VARCHAR since migration 108, not an enum: an enum stores a value it has not been told about as the empty string and says nothing.

is_live.description: started_at is set and ended_at is not. Gate the Join button on this, never on `approved` - approved only means the date is agreed, and a link handed out then is an invitation to wait in an empty room. Consultations have no end time recorded, so unlike a package session there is no clock gate here: a person starts and ends them.

has_zoom.description: update-7 (NEW): a Zoom room has existed for this consultation. Sticky, exactly as on `AvailabilitySlot`.

zoom_is_live.description: update-7 (NEW): a Zoom room is open right now. This is what a Join or End button reads.

get.summary: update-14 (NEW): list product categories

update-14 (NEW): منتجات المتجر — products the store sells that are not books.

Two fields say more than they look: `sale_price` null means "not on sale" while 0 means "deliberately free", and `stock` null means "not tracked" while 0 means "out of stock". Reading either missing value as zero would present every product as free and sold out, so the pairs are kept apart end to end - including in the response, which carries `is_stock_tracked` and `is_on_sale` so a card never has to guess.

`effective_price` and `discount_percent` are computed server-side: a sale price that three screens each decide how to apply is a sale price three screens eventually disagree about.

A sale price above the price is refused. Permission: `manage_products`.

An attachment of ANY type may be uploaded through `file`. Every other upload path on this platform names the extensions it accepts, which is right for an avatar and wrong for a product - an owner may attach a CAD drawing, a font, an installer, or something nobody listed in advance. So the rule is inverted: `upload_any_file()` accepts anything EXCEPT what a web server might run, and checks every segment of the name, so `invoice.pdf.php` is refused as well as `shell.php`. That is defensible because uploads/.htaccess already turns the PHP engine off, strips the handlers and refuses to serve executables - the deny-list is the first lock on a door that is already closed, not the only one.

`file` accepts a multipart upload, a base64 data URI of any media type, or a path already on the server. Absent means keep the current file; an explicit null removes it. Send `file_name` alongside a data URI so the extension is not guessed from the mime subtype - guessing it from the subtype is the hole that once let "data:image/php;base64,..." write a webshell.

The stored name on disk is always generated and is never the uploaded one. The response carries has_file, file_name, file_extension, file_size, file_size_label and file_is_public.

get.summary: update-14 (NEW): the store — products and standalone books in one list
get.description:
update-14 (NEW): المتجر — one shelf, two kinds of thing on it.

Products and standalone books (those tied to no course and no unit) come back in ONE list, in one shape, under one sort. They are not merged in the database - a book has a file, a subject and a reader, and a product has stock and a sale price and none of the rest - so they are brought together here, at the one place that has to show them together.

Every entry carries `item_type` ('product' or 'book') and an `id` that is only unique WITHIN its own type. A client must key on the pair. That is stated rather than hidden behind a synthetic id, because an id that silently means two different things in two tables is how a cart buys the wrong row.

Auth is optional: a visitor sees what is on sale, and a signed-in student additionally sees `own` / `is_locked` on the books they already hold.

`type=product` or `type=book` narrows to one kind. `category_id` narrows to one PRODUCT category and therefore excludes books, which have none - said back in `applied_filters.books_excluded_reason` rather than left for somebody to work out from a suddenly shorter list. `sort`: newest (default), oldest, price_asc, price_desc, name.

Without migration 127 this returns the books it always returned rather than failing - a half-deployed server should still have a shop.

A product may carry an attachment. The store always reports `has_file`, `file_name`, `file_extension` and `file_size_label`, but `file_path` comes back ONLY when the product has `file_is_public = 1` - a digital product's file handed out on the shop front has been given away, and there is no checkout yet to gate it behind.

update-13 (NEW): تقرير المبيعات - revenue over a range, per source, per day, and per item.

Nothing about "what counts as revenue" is defined a second time here, so this report cannot drift from the dashboard's figure.

Returns `summary` (total, orders, average_order, daily_average), `sources` (each revenue door with its own total and order count, highest first), `daily` (one bucket per calendar day, summed across the sources), and `top_items` (up to 20 courses, packages and books by revenue).

get.summary: update-13 (NEW): payroll and deductions report
get.description:
update-13 (NEW): تقرير الرواتب والخصومات - a payslip-shaped row per teacher for the period.

The wallet already held every figure needed: `teacher_wallet_transactions` is written by the attendance run (an earning per class held, a fine per late arrival or absence) and by admin adjustments and approved appeals. What was missing was reading it per PERIOD instead of as a running balance - an owner paying monthly cannot pay out of a lifetime total, and the existing wallet endpoints only ever gave a balance and a ledger.

The money is taken from the ledger rather than recomputed from the pay rate times the hours: the ledger is what the teacher was actually credited, including any correction an admin has since made, and a report that disagrees with the wallet is a report nobody can pay from.

Each row: `earnings`, `fines`, `refunds`, `adjustments`, `net`, the entry counts behind them, `sessions_held` / `sessions_late` / `sessions_absent` / `minutes_late` from the attendance side of the same classes, the `pay_model` and `pay_rate` in force, `wallet_balance`, `is_attendance_suspended`, and `pending_appeals` - a disputed deduction is still deducted while the appeal is open, so a row that does not say one is pending invites paying a figure that is about to change. `statistics` totals the page-independent figures across the whole filtered range.

Permission: `manage_wallets`, NOT `manage_reports` - an admin trusted to read attendance is not automatically trusted to read what every teacher is paid.

post.summary: update-4 (CHANGED): Student login - now device-limited
post.description:
update-1: response now also includes is_subscribed on the student object (same computation as the one already returned by the profile endpoint: true if the student has at least one accessible course via get_student_accessible_entities()).

=== update-4 (BREAKING FOR CLIENTS): DEVICE LIMIT ===

An account may only be signed in from a limited number of devices - one by default. One set of credentials shared around a class was the cheapest way to give a paid course away, and nothing noticed it before.

CLIENT ACTION, REQUIRED: send a `device_id` with every login (body field, or the `X-Device-Id` header). It must be an id the client generates ONCE and keeps - a random uuid in localStorage is enough. Do NOT generate a fresh one per login: the server counts devices, so a new id every time burns through the student's slots immediately. Optional `device_name` and `platform` are what an admin sees in the devices list, so send something human.

While the limit is enabled, a login with NO device id is REFUSED with `error_code: device_id_required`. Letting an unidentified client through would make the whole limit decorative - anyone could drop the field for unlimited sessions.

TWO NEW REFUSALS, both HTTP 200 with `status: "error"` and an `error_code` to branch on:
- `device_id_required` - the client sent no device id.
- `device_limit_reached` - the account is already at its ceiling. The response also carries `max_devices` and `active_devices`. This is NOT a wrong-password error and must not be shown as one: the message tells the student to contact support, because only an admin can free a slot (POST /admin/students/devices/reset).

A device that has signed in before reuses its own slot, so signing in again from the same browser is always allowed.

ON EVERY LATER REQUEST: the access token now carries the device id, and the student auth middleware re-checks that the device is still authorised. A revoked device gets HTTP 401 with `error_code: device_revoked` - treat that as a hard logout, not as a refresh-the-token signal. POST /auth/refresh is gated the same way and answers 403 with the same code, so a revoked device cannot mint itself fresh tokens.

Tokens issued BEFORE this change carry no device id and are left alone, so turning the limit on does not sign out everyone already logged in.

A parent viewing their child (POST /parent/auth/login-as-student) mints a student token with no device id: it does not consume one of the child's slots and is never blocked by the child's limit.

TURNING IT OFF: set `site_settings.student_device_limit_enabled` to `0`. Devices are still recorded, but nothing is refused - use this if a client that cannot be updated yet has to keep working.

update-4 (CHANGED): subject to the login limit when `login_lockout_enabled` is on (migration 074). After `max_login_attempts` failures the response is `error_code: login_locked` with `retry_after_minutes`, and the CORRECT password is refused too until the lock expires. Counted per (email + IP + role), so an attacker can only ever lock out their own address - not the account holder's. The lock expires on its own; an admin can release every lock with POST /admin/login-attempts/clear. Ships OFF.

update-4 (CHANGED): THE EMAIL VERIFICATION GATE IS GONE FOR STUDENTS. Sign-up no longer sends a code and the email itself is optional, so `is_email_verified = 0` is an ordinary state rather than a blocked one - every account created before this change sits at 0, and refusing those would have locked out exactly the students removing verification was meant to let in. The response therefore never returns `requires_email_verification` for a student. Teachers, parents and admins keep their own gates; this is a student-only change.

device_id.description: update-4: REQUIRED while the device limit is enabled. An id the client generates once and KEEPS (a uuid in localStorage). A fresh id per login burns through the student's device slots. May also be sent as the `X-Device-Id` header.

update-4 (NEW): applies a discount code to this grant. THIS is where a code is spent - the redemption is recorded against the new subscription and the code's `used_count` goes up. An invalid code does NOT cancel the grant: the access was requested deliberately, so the subscription is still created and the failure is reported in the response's `discount` object.

Only a course or a package carries a price, so there was nothing to reduce; the old behaviour still recorded a redemption of 0.00, which spent one of the code's uses and, with `once_per_student`, burnt that code for that student permanently in exchange for no discount. post.summary: update-10 (CHANGED): create consultation slots - now from a list of dates, and with an optional hourly price
post.description:
update-10 (NEW FIELD `dates`): the days can now be an explicit list instead of a weekly pattern.

`dates` takes an array of `YYYY-MM-DD` strings - the days somebody picked on a calendar. They need not share a weekday, need not repeat, and need no end date. When it is present, `days` and `end_date` are ignored.

The old form is untouched and still works exactly as it did: leave `dates` out, send `days` (weekday names) and `end_date`, and every repeat up to that date is created. It was the only form available, and it could only describe a run that falls on the same weekday every week - which most consultation timetables do not, because a week gets skipped for a holiday and two days get added before an exam.

Both forms are held to the same window: nothing before today, nothing more than 180 days ahead, at most 200 slots in one call. A date outside it is REFUSED by name rather than quietly dropped - an admin who picks twelve dates and is given nine has no way to tell which three went missing.

update-10 (NEW FIELD `price_per_hour`): optional, and blank is not zero. An empty value means the consultation is not priced, which is what every consultation on the platform was before this; a `0` means it is deliberately free. The two are stored and served apart. A negative or non-numeric value is refused. Needs migration 124; without it the field is accepted and ignored rather than failing.

---

update-2 (Teacher): companion to the existing single-slot POST /teacher/consultations. Instead of creating one dated slot, this materializes one consultation_slots row PER matching calendar date for every selected weekday between today and end_date (inclusive) — e.g. days=[Saturday,Thursday] with end_date next month creates one slot for every upcoming Saturday and every upcoming Thursday up to that date, all at the same slot_time. Safety caps: end_date cannot be more than 180 days out, and a single call cannot generate more than 200 dates total (split into multiple calls if needed). Any date that would collide with an existing (teacher_id, slot_time, slot_date) slot is silently skipped, not duplicated or erroring the whole request — the response reports how many were created vs skipped. Exactly ONE notification is sent for the whole batch (not one per generated slot).

update-6 (CHANGED): accepts an optional `meeting_link`, written to every slot the run creates (migration 107).

update-10 (NEW FIELDS on every consultation slot): `price_per_hour` (a number, or null when nobody has priced it) and `is_free` (true only when a price was set and it is zero). Reading a missing price as 0 would show every slot created before update-10 as a giveaway, which is why the two are separate fields.

post.description:
update-3 (NEW, Section 10). The teacher's way to avoid being fined for a class they already know they will miss or be late to. The request always goes to the ADMIN for review (PUT /admin/attendance/exceptions) - never to another teacher.

WHY IT MATTERS: once approved, that occurrence is marked `is_excused = 1`, which (a) suppresses the automatic fine and (b) keeps it out of the monthly unauthorized-absence counter that would otherwise eventually set `is_attendance_suspended = 1`. 6. there must be no OTHER still-pending request from this same teacher for this same (session_id, occurrence_date), else `request_already_pending`. Note this only blocks duplicates while one is pending - after a rejection the teacher may file again.

post.description:
update-3: this pre-existing endpoint gained TWO behaviors. It is documented here for the first time because both are breaking-ish for clients.

1) NEW HARD TIME GATE. The call is REJECTED with `session_start_too_early` if it arrives more than 5 minutes before the session's scheduled `start_time`. In other words the allowed window opens at start_time minus 5 minutes and never closes (starting late is permitted - and is exactly what produces a 'late' record). The 5 minutes is a fixed constant, NOT the configurable `teacher_grace_minutes` (which governs the opposite side: how late is still 'present').
CLIENT ACTION: the teacher app must surface this message as an alert and keep the Start button disabled until the window opens. And because this error is returned with HTTP 200 and `status: 'error'` in the body, any client that shows a success toast purely on a 2xx will show the error text inside a green toast - branch on the body's `status`.

2) IT IS NOW THE TEACHER'S CHECK-IN. On the FIRST successful call for a given date the server records `teacher_session_attendance` for that occurrence: lateness = now minus start_time in minutes (floored at 0); status = `present` while within `teacher_grace_minutes`, `late` beyond it. If the teacher is `late`, has NO approved late_notice for that occurrence, and `teacher_late_fine_per_minute` > 0, a `fine` ledger row of minutes_late x rate is written immediately and the teacher is notified of the deduction. The subscribed students are also notified that the teacher has joined.
IDEMPOTENT: repeat calls the same day do not re-record, re-fine or re-notify.

There is intentionally no separate teacher check-in endpoint - this is it.

post.summary: update-3 (CHANGED): Teacher asks the admin to reschedule a session - now capped per month, and the new time is genuinely optional
post.description:
update-3: two changes to this pre-existing endpoint.

1) MONTHLY CAP. Before inserting, the server counts this teacher's reschedule requests created since the 1st of the current month. If that count already reaches `teacher_max_reschedule_per_month` from the HR policy, the request is refused with `max_reschedule_requests_reached` ('تم الوصول للحد الأقصى من طلبات التأجيل المسموح بها هذا الشهر'). Note the counter is on requests SUBMITTED, not requests approved - a rejected request still consumes one slot.

2) BUGFIX - `new_start_time` / `new_end_time` are truly optional now. The code always treated them as optional (a reschedule may move only the DAY and keep the same time), but the DB columns were NOT NULL, so omitting them crashed with a raw SQL error "Column 'new_start_time' cannot be null". Migration 062 makes both columns nullable. Omitting them now correctly means 'keep the original time'.

update-3: `session_attendance.status` only ever holds 'present' / 'absent' / 'late'; an authorised absence is stored as status='absent' PLUS the separate `is_excused` flag (added by migration 060). This endpoint previously ignored that flag, so an absence the admin had explicitly approved was reported to the parent as a plain absence.

Now the flag is folded into the reported status: an excused row is emitted with `status = 'excused'` (its own bucket in the counters and its own label), and every row additionally carries the raw boolean `is_excused`.

Despite the path, this is a STUDENT token route: the id sent has to be the signed-in student's own, and any other is refused as unauthorized.

get.summary: update-3 (CHANGED): Student's subscriptions now expose is_frozen / freeze_reason
get.description:
update-3: every subscription object returned anywhere in the API (student, admin list, admin details - all three copies of the resolver were updated) now carries two new fields:
- `is_frozen` (boolean): true when `is_active = 0` AND the subscription has NOT merely expired.
- `freeze_reason` (string|null): a ready-to-display localized explanation when frozen, null otherwise.

This is unambiguous because `student_subscriptions.is_active` is set to 0 by exactly ONE code path in the entire backend - the attendance auto-freeze. Expiry is tracked separately via `end_date`, and admins do not toggle this column by hand.

CLIENT ACTION: where the UI used to print 'غير فعال' (Inactive) for is_active = 0, print 'مجمد' (Frozen) instead when is_frozen is true, show `freeze_reason`, and offer a contact-support action. 'Inactive' is now reserved for genuinely expired/ended subscriptions.

get.summary: update-3 (CHANGED): 'My Courses' now KEEPS frozen courses in the list, flagged instead of hidden
get.description:
update-3: previously, when a student's subscription was frozen, the courses it granted simply vanished from this list - indistinguishable from never having subscribed, which was confusing and made the student think their purchase was lost.

Now the list is the UNION of (a) courses the student can currently access and (b) courses whose only grant is a frozen subscription. Every returned course object gains:
- `is_frozen` (boolean): true ONLY for courses in group (b) - i.e. it is false for a course the student can still reach through some other active grant, even if a different frozen subscription also covered it.
- `freeze_reason` (string|null).

CLIENT ACTION: render frozen courses with a clear 'مجمد' (Frozen) badge, HIDE the 'Continue course' action (the student genuinely cannot open its content), and replace it with a contact-support action. Actual content access is enforced server-side independently - see the access-control fix noted on GET /courses/show.

get.summary: update-3, update-4 (ENHANCED), update-8 (FIXED): List exams available to the student - now includes STANDALONE exams (no course/unit/subject) offered to every student, with `is_public` and `has_time_limit` on every row
get.description:
update-8 (FIX): with no `course_id` in the request at all (the student's general "my exams" tab), unit-scoped exams are now excluded by default too, exactly like case 1 below already did when `course_id` was passed - previously the exclusion only kicked in when `course_id` was explicitly sent, so a unit exam for a subscribed course leaked into the unfiltered listing. `include_unit_exams`/`with_unit_exams` still opts back in, with or without `course_id`.

Every exam in the system always has a non-null `course_id` (the creation UI requires picking a course first, whether the exam is a whole-course exam or a unit exam - `unit_id` is only set for the latter, on top of the same course_id). Because of that, this endpoint treats `course_id` requests differently depending on `include_unit_exams` - READ THIS BEFORE CALLING IT WITH course_id:

1) `course_id` ALONE (default, `include_unit_exams` unset/`0`/`false`) -> returns ONLY whole-course exams for that course (`unit_id IS NULL`). Unit exams belonging to that course are DELIBERATELY excluded - this is the default precisely so a course-details screen doesn't unexpectedly show unit exams mixed in with the course's own exam.
2) `course_id` + `unit_id` -> returns exams for that ONE specific unit only (existing, unchanged behavior) - `include_unit_exams` is ignored in this case.
3) `course_id` + `include_unit_exams=1` (alias: `with_unit_exams=1`) -> returns the COMBINED list: the whole-course exam(s) AND every unit exam under that course, mixed together in one array. Use this for an aggregated 'all exams in this course' screen/tab - each item still carries its own `unit_id`/`unit` object (null for the whole-course ones) so the client can group or label them.
4) `course_id` + `include_unit_exams=only` -> returns UNIT EXAMS ONLY for that course (`unit_id IS NOT NULL`), EXCLUDING the whole-course exam(s) entirely. Use this for a screen that lists only per-unit exams, with no whole-course exam mixed in.

`unit_id` alone (no course_id) and `subject_id` alone keep their original, unrelated behavior - filtering directly on that column, unaffected by any of the above.

Access control (unrelated to the scoping above): an exam is only returned if the student is subscribed to its subject or its course - a student with no subscriptions at all gets an empty list immediately, before any of the filters run.

update-4 (SORTING): results are now explicitly ordered - previously this endpoint had NO ORDER BY at all, so the order was undefined (effectively storage-engine dependent) and could silently change between calls. The default is now NEWEST FIRST (by `created_at` then `id`, descending). Use the `sort` parameter to reverse it.

update-4 (VISIBILITY): only exams with `is_active` (= `show_to_students`) equal to 1 are ever returned here - an exam an admin or teacher has hidden via PUT /admin/exams or PUT /teacher/exams (`is_active: 0`) disappears from this list immediately and unconditionally, regardless of any other filter in this request.

STANDALONE EXAMS: an exam with no course, no unit and no subject is returned to EVERY student, including one with no subscriptions at all, and carries is_public = 1. has_time_limit = 0 means duration_minutes is 0 and the exam has no countdown.

update-4 (CHANGED): with no sort requested the list now comes back in the content team's order (`order_num ASC, id ASC`) rather than newest-first, so the student's exam tab matches what the dashboard shows. Passing `sort`, `sort_by` or `order` still sorts by `created_at` as before - an explicitly requested sort wins over the manual one.

update-4 (CHANGED): a unit exam that was saved without a `course_id` - rows created before that was enforced carry only the unit - now has it filled in from the unit. Every endpoint that embeds an exam summary gets this, which is what lets a client offer "back to the course this exam belongs to" for every exam rather than only the ones entered after the fix.

- unset / `0` / `false` (default): whole-course/standalone exams only - unit exams excluded.
- `1` / `true`: COMBINED - whole-course/standalone exam(s) + every unit exam the student has access to.
- `only` (aliases: `unit_only`, `units_only`): UNIT EXAMS ONLY - excludes the whole-course/standalone exam(s) entirely.

get.summary: update-4 (REWRITE): Teacher dashboard home - fully real, wired to every teacher-relevant system
get.description:
Complete rewrite of this endpoint. The previous implementation was demo/placeholder code: every KPI had a hardcoded fallback number (e.g. a fake '24512 students' / '$84254 revenue') that was returned whenever the real query came back empty or zero, a 7-month chart with fixed fake numbers, and 3 hardcoded 'recent activity' rows naming students who don't exist in this database. NONE of that remains - every field below is a live, real query against this teacher's own data, and a genuinely empty result now correctly reads as zero/empty rather than being papered over with a fake number.

This is the single aggregate call for a teacher app's home/dashboard screen, pulling together:
- Profile snapshot + real rating/reviews (`teacher`).
- Top-line KPI cards (`kpis`).
- Section 10 wallet balance and effective pay rate (`wallet`) - same numbers as GET /teacher/wallet.
- Today's full schedule with live status per session (`today`) - same session objects as GET /teacher/sessions.
- Every action currently awaiting this teacher, broken out per source, so the UI can deep-link each one (`pending_actions`): ungraded homework submissions, ungraded exam attempts, incoming student reschedule requests, this teacher's own pending Section 10 exception requests and deduction appeals, and pending consultation bookings.
- A preview of up to 6 owned courses/packages with real student counts (`my_courses`).
- The next 5 approved+booked consultations (`upcoming_consultations`).
- The 5 most recent notifications (`recent_notifications`).

Both GET /teacher/home and GET /teacher/content/home hit the exact same handler (`teacherHome`) - they are not two different implementations, just two paths that existed already.

get.summary: MOVED FROM `old / Admin / Dashboard`. Changed again in update-5: Sales now include manual and WhatsApp sales, a cancelled manual sale is excluded, and packages are counted apart from courses. update-4 (EXPANDED): Dashboard statistics - counts, sales, per-course sales, yearly charts and recent activity
get.description:
Everything the admin dashboard home page needs, in one call.

update-4 additions (previously this endpoint returned only the `statistics` counts):
- `statistics.courses` - course count, alongside the existing entity counts.
- `sales` - total / today / this month / this year revenue, plus a per-channel breakdown.
- `top_courses` - sales and revenue per course, best seller first.
- `charts.sales_by_month` and `charts.students_by_month` - always exactly 12 entries (January to December), including months with no data, so a chart can be rendered without filling gaps client-side.
- `recent_activity` - newest platform events, each with a `link` to the page that handles it.

No database change was needed for any of this: every figure is derived from tables that already exist.

=== update-5 ===

`sales` gains a third source, `manual_subscriptions`: a sale closed over WhatsApp or in cash used to be recorded as a subscription with no price, so it appeared in no revenue figure at all. It is now priced (migration 099) and counted.

A manual sale that was later cancelled no longer counts - `cancelled_at IS NULL` was missing, so cancelling a sale left its money in the total.

`statistics` separates `kind = 'package'` from ordinary courses; the course count used to swallow the packages.

post.summary: update-4 (NEW): Sign a student out of every session
post.description:
Ends every session the student has open, everywhere, immediately.

DIFFERENT FROM RESETTING DEVICES, and both are worth having:
- POST /admin/students/devices/reset frees the SLOTS, so a NEW device can sign in.
- this ends every SESSION, so the SAME device simply has to sign in again.

The second is what you want when a phone goes missing: end the sessions without also costing the student the device slot they will want back in an hour. Send `revoke_devices: true` to do both at once.

It also reaches sessions device revocation cannot see. Rather than looking for a device id, it stamps `students.sessions_revoked_at` and every token issued before that moment is refused - so tokens minted before devices existed, or while the limit was switched off, die too.

Both the auth middleware and POST /auth/refresh enforce it, so a signed-out session cannot refresh its way back in. Clients get `error_code: session_revoked` (HTTP 401 on a normal call, 403 on refresh) and should treat it as a hard logout. A login AFTER the cutoff is unaffected.

post.description:
The student using a code rather than previewing it. There is no payment gateway in this platform, so using a code cannot mean paying with it: this PINS the code to the course or package the student wants. The claim is stored as a `pending` row on `discount_code_redemptions`, the code's `used_count` is NOT touched, and the admin's later grant is what turns it into a real discount.

Why this matters to a client: after a successful apply, the student does not have to relay the code to support by hand. POST /admin/subscriptions with NO `discount_code` in the body now looks the student's pending claims up itself and honours the first still-valid one for the granted courses.

Idempotent per student + code + course: pressing the button twice re-reads the same claim and re-prices it instead of stacking rows. Requires a logged-in student - an anonymous visitor has nothing to pin a code to, and gets an error rather than a silent no-op.

Rejected for the same reasons as a check (inactive, not started, expired, fully used, wrong course, already used by this student), and the message explains which.

post.summary: MOVED FROM `update-4 / Student - Auth`. update-4 (CHANGED): Student registration - email optional, no verification code, straight in. update-7: a profile picture can be sent with the sign-up itself
post.description:
update-4 (CHANGED): refused with `error_code: registration_disabled` while the `registration_enabled` setting is 0 (migration 074).

Checked before anything is read or written, so a closed platform never half-creates an account and never sends a verification email for one that will not exist. Existing accounts are unaffected - only new sign-ups are closed. The message shown is the admin-editable `registration_disabled_message_ar` / `_en`.

Teacher registration is deliberately NOT covered: a teacher account does not work until an admin approves it, so it is already gated by a person.

update-4 (CHANGED): THE EMAIL IS OPTIONAL. `students.email` was NOT NULL with a UNIQUE key, which is why the form could not simply stop requiring it - an empty string would have been stored and the second student without an email would have collided with the first. Migration 095 makes the column nullable, because MySQL allows any number of NULLs in a UNIQUE index. Required now: `name` and `password`, plus EITHER an email OR a phone number - an account with neither would be created and immediately unreachable, so that case is refused with `error_code: email_or_phone_required`. `academic_year_id` and `study_language` were already optional in the handler; only the form was demanding them.

update-4 (CHANGED): NO VERIFICATION CODE. Nothing is generated and nothing is sent. The row is written with `is_email_verified = 1` - not left at 0 - so that screens still reading the column do not show a permanent "unverified" badge against an account nobody will ever be asked to verify. The response no longer carries a `verification` object; it carries `requires_email_verification: false` (always) and the usual `tokens`, so the student is signed in by the act of signing up.

update-4 (CHANGED): `default_phone_dial_code` in site_settings is seeded to 961 (Lebanon) by migration 095. The setting already existed and had never been given a value, so the hard-coded fallback behind it - Egypt's 20 - was what a number typed without a country code became.

=== update-7 ===

The account's picture can now be set AT SIGN-UP, in `image`, exactly as `PUT /user/student/auth/profile` already accepted it: a `data:image/...;base64,` payload, a multipart file, or a path that has already been uploaded. `avatar`, `photo`, `profile_image`, `picture` and `file` are accepted as aliases, in the body or as the multipart field name.

The field was technically read before this, but stored verbatim - an app sending a picture the way every other screen sends one wrote a whole base64 payload into a column that holds a filename, so the picture only appeared once the profile screen had been opened a second time to set it again. A caller that was already sending an uploaded path is unaffected: such a value still passes through unchanged.

Still optional. An account with no picture is normal, and one can be added later from the profile screen.

phone_country_code.description: Aliases: `country_code`, `dial_code`. A number that already carries its own code wins over it.

image.description: update-7: base64 data URL, an already-uploaded path, or a multipart file. Aliases: `avatar`, `photo`, `profile_image`, `picture`, `file`.

get.summary: update-9 (CHANGED): Read every site setting
get.description:
update-9 (NEW KEYS): the three marketing sections on the home page - the limited offer, the intro video and the picture carousel.

All of this was written inside the website's own code: the creatives were files committed into its repository and the wording lived in its translation files, so changing a discount figure or a campaign picture meant a developer and a deploy. Migration 123 copies the live wording and media paths into `site_settings` unchanged, so nothing about the page moves when it runs.

Switches, '0' or '1', each defaulting to ON when the key was never written (these sections are live today, and adding a switch must not be what turns them off): `promo_offer_enabled`, `promo_video_enabled`, `promo_gallery_enabled`.

Media, stored as plain URLs or site-relative paths and served unchanged: `promo_offer_image`, `promo_video_url`, `promo_video_poster`.

Copy, stored as an `_ar` / `_en` pair per key: `promo_offer_badge`, `promo_offer_amount` (the large discount figure - Arabic-Indic digits on the Arabic site, Western digits on the English one), `promo_offer_title`, `promo_offer_subtitle`, `promo_offer_cta`, `promo_offer_image_alt`, `promo_video_title`, `promo_video_subtitle`, `promo_video_cta`, `promo_gallery_title`, `promo_gallery_subtitle`.

Lists, one JSON array per key: `promo_offer_pills` and `promo_video_points` hold `{text_ar, text_en}` objects; `promo_gallery_items` holds `{image, caption_ar, caption_en}` objects.

An empty value is not an empty section: the website falls back to the wording and the files it shipped with, so an installation that has never touched these keys renders exactly as it always did.

---

update-4 (CHANGED): now requires the `manage_settings` permission (migration 074).

These endpoints previously had NO permission check at all - any admin account, however narrowly scoped, could read and rewrite every key in `site_settings`, the registration switch and the login limit included. The permission is granted to nobody by the migration, so it has to be handed over deliberately.

The store is key/value: GET returns every key as a flat object, POST takes only the keys being changed.

update-4 (NEW KEYS): the scrolling announcement bar at the top of the website.

`announcement_bar_enabled` - '0' or '1', validated like the other switches.

`announcement_bar_items` - ONE key holding a JSON array of `{text_ar, text_en}` objects, not a fixed set of columns, so an admin can list as many announcements as they want (maximum 20). A malformed value is REFUSED rather than silently dropped - saving "successfully" while the bar quietly stops showing anything is the worse outcome. An empty string is accepted and means no announcements.

On the public side the key is resolved before it is served: each item collapses to the single string matching the request language (falling back to the other language when one side is blank), blanks are dropped, and the result is a flat array of strings. update-4 (CHANGED): now requires the `manage_settings` permission (migration 074).

These endpoints previously had NO permission check at all - any admin account, however narrowly scoped, could read and rewrite every key in `site_settings`, the registration switch and the login limit included. The permission is granted to nobody by the migration, so it has to be handed over deliberately.

The store is key/value: GET returns every key as a flat object, POST takes only the keys being changed.

POST also validates the keys that have a contract, and rejects the WHOLE request rather than saving part of it - a half-saved settings form leaves the platform in a state nobody chose. Rules: `whatsapp_number` must be international and is refused if it starts with a zero (Egypt's local 01xxxxxxxxx is 11 digits and would pass any plain length check while opening a chat with nobody); `support_email` must parse; social links must start with http(s)://; `max_login_attempts` 1-50; `login_lockout_minutes` 1-1440; `max_devices_per_student` 1-50; the switches `registration_enabled`, `login_lockout_enabled` and `student_device_limit_enabled` must be '0' or '1'; and BOTH `registration_disabled_message_ar` and `registration_disabled_message_en` must be non-blank, since a refused user is served whichever one matches their language.

Everything else - the landing page copy, the stats labels - stays free text. The validator is deliberately not a whitelist, or the website editor would silently stop saving.

update-4 (NEW KEYS): the scrolling announcement bar at the top of the website.

`announcement_bar_enabled` - '0' or '1', validated like the other switches.

`announcement_bar_items` - ONE key holding a JSON array of `{text_ar, text_en}` objects, not a fixed set of columns, so an admin can list as many announcements as they want (maximum 20). A malformed value is REFUSED rather than silently dropped - saving "successfully" while the bar quietly stops showing anything is the worse outcome. An empty string is accepted and means no announcements.

On the public side the key is resolved before it is served: each item collapses to the single string matching the request language (falling back to the other language when one side is blank), blanks are dropped, and the result is a flat array of strings. The bar is only shown when it is BOTH enabled and has at least one non-empty item, so a disabled or empty bar never reserves blank space on the page.

update-15: moving the base currency can no longer reprice the platform in silence.

`courses.price` and `course_books.price` are bare numbers. Nothing on the row says which currency they are in - the answer is whatever `base_currency` says today. So changing that setting converted nothing: a course priced at 300 EGP became a course priced at 300 SAR, roughly eight times dearer, with no edit and nothing on screen to show it had happened. Setting the currency back does not undo it either, because the figures were never changed.

A price now reaches the incoming currency one of two ways and no third:
  * it was ALREADY entered for a country that uses that currency, so it is adopted. Matching is on the currency rather than on one country, since several countries share one; where more than one exists the lowest is taken, because over-charging is the worse mistake.
  * the admin TYPED it, sent as `base_currency_prices`.

Anything still without one REFUSES THE WHOLE CHANGE. Nothing is written - not the prices and not the setting - so a refusal leaves the platform exactly as it was, and the response names the items in `base_currency_blocked.missing`.

No conversion is ever invented. An exchange rate picked by the server would put a number in front of a customer that nobody approved.

Store products are outside all of this: `products.currency` is a column on each row, so a product already carries its own currency and the base setting never spoke for it. `course_books` rows DO go through it - their price is a bare number like a course's - and the dashboard labels them "منتج" because that is what the platform sells them as.

Sending `base_currency` through THIS endpoint is what triggers the guard. It lives here rather than behind its own endpoint precisely because a separate endpoint is what would be stepped around by posting the key straight to this one.

`base_currency_prices` carries the typed prices: a map keyed `"course-12"` / `"book-7"`, a list of `{item_type, item_id, price}`, or either of those JSON-encoded as a string. It is consumed by the change and never stored as a setting. Zero is accepted - an item can be given away on purpose - and a negative number is not a price.

On success the response carries `base_currency_change` with `adopted_from_stored` and `adopted_from_entered`. On refusal it is `status: "error"` with `base_currency_blocked`.

update-15 (CHANGED): WHERE THE REQUEST COMES FROM now decides the price.

The country saved on the student used to sit second and beat both live signals, so a student connecting from Germany kept being quoted the base price - `source` came back as `student` and nothing about the connection could outrank it.

The lookup's answer is also no longer written back into `students.country_id`. That stamp turned one connection into a permanent verdict and destroyed the NULL that means "detect it each time", so a stamped student could never return to automatic. Where someone connects from is read per request; where they LIVE is theirs to state, through POST /student/pricing/country.

Trade-off, stated plainly: a student travelling or on a VPN is priced where they are rather than where they live. That was already true of every signed-out visitor, so the old rule only protected signed-in purchases and only half the time.

get.summary: update-4 (NEW): May this admin open the chat?
get.description:
A permission probe, nothing more. The body is always `{status: 'success', message: 'ok'}` - the answer is the status code, 200 or 403.

Chat is not a PHP/MySQL feature: the dashboard talks to Firebase directly, so no backend route ever mediated who could open it. That is the actual reason chat had no permission checkbox - a permission in this codebase is only real because a route enforces it, and no route existed to attach one to. The chat page calls this before it opens a single Firebase connection, and a 403 keeps the chat UI from mounting.

Gated on `manage_chat`.

KNOWN LIMIT, stated plainly: Firebase's own security rules are not scoped per permission, so an admin who already holds valid Firebase credentials and drives the SDK by hand (browser console, hand-crafted request) is not stopped at the data layer - only the dashboard path is. That is weaker than every other permission here, which the database enforces per request. Closing it properly means Firebase custom claims plus matching rules.

Send the COMPLETE list, not a page of it. The dashboard only enables dragging when the table is unfiltered and unsorted, for exactly this reason: a page of ten ids would be stamped 1..10 and silently overwrite the positions of everything else.

Unknown ids are skipped rather than failing the request. Gated on `manage_courses`.

Related: GET /admin/courses now defaults to `order_num ASC, id DESC`, accepts `limit` up to 1000 (the ordering view needs the whole list in one request) and takes `light=1` to trim each row down.

post.summary: update-4 (NEW): Save the teacher's manual order for their own courses
post.description:
NOT the same write as the admin endpoint, deliberately. A teacher only sees their own courses - a subset of a list the admin orders too - so stamping 1..N here would overwrite the positions other teachers' courses hold.

Instead the teacher's own courses keep the exact set of `order_num` slots they already occupy, and only which course sits in which slot changes. Nobody else's position moves.

Every id must be a course the teacher owns (`courses.teacher_id`) or is assigned to (`course_teachers.is_active = 1`); if any id is not, the whole request is refused rather than partly applied.
