post.summary: update-4 (DOCUMENTED): Start - or restart - an exam attempt
post.description:
RETAKING IS UNLIMITED, AND ONLY THE LATEST SITTING IS KEPT. There is at most one attempt row per (exam, student): starting an exam that was already finished REUSES that row - its answers are deleted and its status, scores and timestamps are reset - so the previous result is replaced rather than stacked beside the new one. The `student_reports` row is keyed on that attempt id and rewritten at submit, so no second report appears either. Calling this while an attempt is already `in_progress` returns that attempt untouched, so a refresh does not wipe answers.

update-4 (CHANGED): questions come back ordered by `order_num ASC, id ASC` - the order the teacher arranged them in, and the same order the result screen lists them in. They used to be served by id here while the result used order_num, so a student sat the paper in one sequence and read the result in another.

Access: a standalone exam (no course, unit or subject) is open to every student; any other exam needs a subscription covering its course or subject.

Returns `attempt_id`, the `exam` summary and the `questions` array - MCQ options are included WITHOUT the is_correct flag, for obvious reasons.

get.summary: update-4 (DOCUMENTED): The student's finished attempts
get.description:
Every attempt of this student that is no longer `in_progress`, newest first. One row per exam, since a retake reuses its attempt.

update-4 (CHANGED): this list no longer reveals correct answers. It draws a score and a status per attempt and never renders an answer, so fetching MCQ options and written model answers for every question of every exam a student has ever sat was work for nobody. Each row still carries its `answers` array - every question, with what the student put - but without `options`, `correct_answer`, `correct_option_id` or `model_answer`. Open a single attempt with /student/exams/results/show for those.

get.summary: update-4 (CHANGED): One attempt in full - every question, right answer included
get.description:
update-4 (FIXED): THE RESULT SHOWS THE WHOLE PAPER, NOT ONLY WHAT WAS ANSWERED. The answer list used to be built starting from `exam_attempt_answers`, so a question the student left blank produced no row and simply vanished: someone who answered four of ten saw a four-question paper, with no way to tell what they had skipped or what the answer was - which is most of the reason to look at a result at all. It is built from the exam's questions now, LEFT JOINed to the attempt, ordered by `order_num ASC, id ASC`.

PER ANSWER:
- `is_answered` - 0 for a question the student never touched.
- `is_correct` - stays NULL for a skipped question rather than becoming 0. "Not answered" and "answered wrongly" are different things and a client must not colour them the same; in particular a null `true_false_answer` is not False.
- `score_awarded` - 0 for a skipped question, null while a written answer awaits grading.
- MCQ: `options` (each with `is_correct`), plus `correct_option_id` and `correct_answer_text` spelled out so a client can print "the right answer was X" without scanning the list.
- true/false: `correct_answer` (0/1).
- written: `model_answer` (also mirrored into `correct_answer_text`) - the teacher's model answer, the only thing a student can compare their own text against on a hand-graded question. Null when no model answer was written.

PER ATTEMPT: `questions_count` and `answered_count` alongside the existing score fields.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The attempt id. Alias: `attempt_id`.

put.summary: update-4 (DOCUMENTED): Grade an attempt's written answers (admin)
put.description:
Same handler and same payload as PUT /teacher/exams/attempts, reached with an admin token and gated on `manage_exams`. The admin is not checked for ownership of the exam, which is the only difference.

update-4 (FIXED): grading is an UPSERT, not an UPDATE. It used to write with `UPDATE ... WHERE attempt_id = ? AND question_id = ?`, which was fine while only answered questions were ever listed to a grader. Now that a result lists the whole paper, a teacher can grade a written question the student left blank - and that question has no answer row, so an UPDATE matching nothing reported success and saved neither the mark nor the note. The unique key (attempt_id, question_id) makes the upsert safe.

update-4 (CHANGED): the attempt detail returned here now contains every question of the exam, including the skipped ones - see GET /student/exams/results/show for the shape.

post.summary: update-5 (NEW): Start a card payment with the gateway and get the redirect url
post.description:
Opens a payment at EasyKash for a course, a package or a book and returns the url to send the buyer to.

Three things this does that the earlier flow did not:

1. It charges the price of the BUYER'S country, the same figure the catalogue showed them, instead of the base price.

2. Every attempt gets its own reference, `BX<id>-<8 hex>`, stored in `payment_transactions.gateway_reference` (migration 098). EasyKash consumes a reference permanently per merchant account, and the row id was being reused - which made EVERY checkout fail with `customerReference is already used`.

   CLIENT ACTION: the reference is a STRING. Passing it through `Number()` yields NaN.

3. A discount code and a points balance are applied here too (migration 100). They used to work for bank-transfer payments only and were silently ignored for card payments. The payable amount is computed on the server; an amount sent by the client is not trusted.

When the gateway refuses, its own reason is returned rather than a generic failure - the reason used to be discarded, which left every failure looking identical.

update-18: refuses an item with no price, with error_code `not_for_sale`.

200.description: Payment opened; the body carries the redirect url and the reference.

400.description: The gateway refused. `message` carries ITS reason.

post.summary: update-5 (NEW): Settle a payment from the gateway's own answer
post.description:
Called when the buyer returns from the gateway. The server asks EasyKash what happened and acts on THAT.

It used to believe the browser: a crafted return url was enough to be granted a paid course.

Granting is claimed atomically (`UPDATE ... WHERE status <> 'paid'`), so a confirm that races the gateway's own callback cannot create a second subscription and a second affiliate commission for one payment.

reference.description: The gateway reference, e.g. `BX42-9f3c1ab7`. A string, not a number.

200.description: Settled, or already settled - both answer success.

get.summary: update-5 (NEW): Ask what became of a payment

Reports the stored state, refreshed from the gateway when it is still open.

"Nobody has paid yet" and "the gateway did not answer" are now separate outcomes. They used to arrive as the same error, so a client could not tell a buyer who had simply not finished from an outage.

post.summary: update-5 (NEW): Gateway callback - EasyKash reports a payment here
post.description:
Called by EasyKash, not by any client. Unauthenticated by necessity; the payload is verified instead.

AMOUNT CHECK: the reported amount must be at least the amount owed, with a one-piastre tolerance. Not equality - EasyKash ADDS ITS FEE ON TOP of what was requested (ask it for 2.00 and it reports 3.00), so an equality check would have rejected every genuine payment. A short payment is refused and both figures are logged. If no amount field arrives at all, that is recorded as "not verified" rather than treated as a match.

The grant is claimed atomically, so this and the student's own confirm cannot both grant the same purchase.

A refund reported here withdraws access: it closes the one subscription that payment opened - matched by grant reference and student, not by course - and cancels the affiliate commission only while it is still pending. A commission already paid out is left alone.

requestBody.description: EasyKash's payload. Field names are matched case-insensitively.

Documented here for the update-7 change; the endpoint itself predates this changelog. Every field is optional and only the ones sent are written - an empty body is refused with `no_fields_to_update`.

=== update-7 ===

Changing the email to a DIFFERENT address now sets `is_email_verified` to 0 and sends a verification code to the new address. Before this the flag stayed at 1, so the account went on claiming an address nobody had ever proven belonged to it.

Authentication is OPTIONAL: signed out it is the public catalogue, signed in every row also says whether this student owns it (`own` / `is_subscribed`) and where their purchase request stands (`request_status`).

=== update-7: THE STORE ===

What used to be "books" is now the store, and it sells two kinds of thing. The split is carried by `course_books.file_type`, which already existed:

- `pdf` (or any other extension) - a DIGITAL product. A file, read inside the platform, exactly as a book always was.
- `physical` - a PHYSICAL item: a bag, headphones, a stationery set. It has NO file at all. The student buys it and it is handed over off the platform.

update-12 (NEW): the students a homework in this subject would reach - the list to pick from when aiming one at only some of them.

One aggregate query mirroring the paths a subscription can grant a subject by: the subject named directly, a course that belongs to it, or a teacher who teaches it - each arriving either on the subscription or on the subscription code behind it.

get.summary: update-15 (NEW): what changing the base currency would do
get.description:
update-15: moving the base currency can no longer reprice the platform in silence.

`courses.price` and `course_books.price` are bare numbers. Nothing on the row says which currency they are in - the answer is whatever `base_currency` says today. So changing that setting converted nothing: a course priced at 300 EGP became a course priced at 300 SAR, roughly eight times dearer, with no edit and nothing on screen to show it had happened. Setting the currency back does not undo it either, because the figures were never changed.

A price now reaches the incoming currency one of two ways and no third:
  * it was ALREADY entered for a country that uses that currency, so it is adopted. Matching is on the currency rather than on one country, since several countries share one; where more than one exists the lowest is taken, because over-charging is the worse mistake.
  * the admin TYPED it, sent as `base_currency_prices`.

Anything still without one REFUSES THE WHOLE CHANGE. Nothing is written - not the prices and not the setting - so a refusal leaves the platform exactly as it was, and the response names the items in `base_currency_blocked.missing`.

No conversion is ever invented. An exchange rate picked by the server would put a number in front of a customer that nobody approved.

Store products are outside all of this: `products.currency` is a column on each row, so a product already carries its own currency and the base setting never spoke for it. `course_books` rows DO go through it - their price is a bare number like a course's - and the dashboard labels them "منتج" because that is what the platform sells them as.

Read-only, and the confirmation screen calls it before anything is saved.

Returns `adoptable` (items with a stored price in the target currency, each with `current_price` and `new_price`), `missing` (items with none, which must be given one), `missing_by_kind` counted as package / normal / book, and both counts. `is_change` is false when the target is already the base currency.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: The three-letter code being moved to. Must be an ACTIVE currency.

get.summary: update-12: list homework (teacher)
get.description:
update-12 (CHANGED): homework can be aimed at particular students.

A homework row carried a subject and nothing else, so publishing one handed it to every student subscribed to that subject. A teacher wanting to set extra practice for the three students who are behind had no way to say so.

  * NO students chosen -> the homework is for everyone subscribed to the subject. This is exactly the old behaviour, and what every homework that already exists still does.
  * students chosen -> only they see it, and only they may submit to it.

Targeting NARROWS an audience and never widens one: a student still has to be subscribed to the subject, so no row here hands anyone access they did not already have.

Wire-level: `student_ids`, `students` and `is_targeted` are ADDED to the homework object. Nothing was removed or renamed, and a client that ignores all three behaves exactly as it does today.

Needs migration 126, which is applied. Before it ran, targeting did not exist and homework stayed visible to the whole subject rather than anything breaking.

Scoped to the signed-in teacher: they may only ever touch their own rows.

Each row carries `student_ids`, `students` (id and name) and `is_targeted`.

post.summary: update-16 (BREAKING): a file upload that now needs a token
post.description:
update-16 (BREAKING): this endpoint now requires authentication.

It took a file from anybody at all - no token, no role - wrote it to the server's disk and handed back the URL it is served from. That is free hosting on this domain for whatever a stranger wants to put there, and it was the only unguarded write on the API.

It is guarded by `anyAuthMiddleware`, the same guard `/upload/audio` already used, which accepts ANY of the four roles - admin, teacher, student or parent. So every signed-in caller keeps working unchanged and only anonymous requests are refused.

What breaks: anything calling this without an Authorization header. The one caller in the dashboards already sends one.

Takes the file as a multipart part, or as a base64 data URI under any of `file`, `image`, `document`, `attachment` or `media`. Returns `file_path` (what to store) and `file_url` (the absolute URL).
